newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower in nervous market.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower in nervous market.

text.p: Italian stocks closed lower on profit-taking on Thursday in a nervous, hesitant market after a session of sporadic movements.

"It was an indecisive market for much of the day, hovering between a correction downwards and a new move up," one trader said. "But the fact that volumes contracted when the bourse index declined shows underlying sentiment isn't too bad."
Telecoms, Fiat and Gemina particularly saw selling.
The All-share Mibtel index closed down 0.56 pct at 12,565 but off a low at 12,509. The Mib30 blue chip index ended off 0.58 pct at 18,717 after an 18,609 low.
Telecoms were all lower, with Telecom Italia off 2.34 percent at 4,585 lire and mobile phone operator TIM down a modest 0.1 percent to 4,768 but Stet holding lost 2.49 percent to 7,799 lire.
Financial holding Gemina shed 2.71 percent to 1,006 lire in what traders described as a technical correction after recent gains. Fiat fell 2.67 percent to 5,276 "but in lower volumes".

Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's television and advertising group Mediaset gained 2.64 percent to 7,491 lire on signs of less conflict with the centre-left government over the thorny question of TV sector regulation.
Insurance and financial services group Mediolanum, partly owned by Berlusconi, gained 4.26 percent to 18,892 lire, the leading blue chip gainer.
Dealers said the stock benefited from good inflows into investment funds, for which January data were published today.
Banks were mixed, with Banca Commerciale Italiana up 0.45 percent to 3,579 and San Paolo up 1.07 percent to 11,825. But Ambroveneto lost 2.5 percent to 4,677.
Energy group ENI slipped 0.3 percent to 9,188 and Olivetti lost 1.27 percent to 667.6 lire.
